newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-AJAX BEAT ATLETICO 3-2 IN ACTION-PACKED CLASSIC.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AJAX BEAT ATLETICO 3-2 IN ACTION-PACKED CLASSIC.

text.p: Four-times European champions Ajax earned a semifinal showdown with the Juventus side that deprived them of a fifth title last season by beating Atletico Madrid 3-2 in an epic quarter-final tie on Wednesday.
Goalkeeper Edwin van der Sar was the hero for the Dutch in the 4-3 aggregate win after salvaging extra time with a 75th- minute penalty save.

Atletico faced an uphill battle, needing to score twice, after substitute striker Dani scored a superb goal in extra time, and despite pulling one back went down to a last-gasp effort from Tijani Babangida.
Ajax coach Louis van Gaal admitted that the Spaniards had at times outplayed his side after starting poorly.
"We should have gone 2-0 up in the first half hour," said Van Gaal, who had warned before the game of the danger posed by Spanish international striker Kiko.
Kiko fulfilled Van Gaal's predictions with a spirited performance and put his side ahead in the 29th minute with a powerful shot after Carlos Aguilera had found space down the right.
Moments later Atletico missed a chance to go further ahead when Diego Simeone brushed the post from close range after a mix-up at a corner.
The home side could also count themselves unlucky not to have been awarded a penalty just before half time when Delfi Geli appeared to be brought down by van der Sar.

The Dutch hit straight back after the break when a defensive muddle gave Jari Litmanen time to cross to an unmarked Ronald de Boer, who headed the equaliser which slipped through the hands of Atletico keeper Jose Molina.
Atletico had the best of a hectic and open second half but mistakes at the back meant that some of the best chances fell to the visitors.
One such error in the 70th minute let in Litmanen, but his shot was cleared off the line with Molina beaten.
Moments later Kiko headed a Pantic free-kick inches wide, and Kiko was again involved in setting up Juan Esnaider for a shot that Van der Sar saved well with his feet.

Kiko seemed to have rounded off a fine game with less than 15 minutes on the clock when his neat turn forced substitute defender John Veldman into a rash challenge and the referee pointed to the spot.
But Van der Sar completed a miserable evening for Esnaider by diving to his right to save the Argentine's penalty.
Esnaider was booked for a horrible challenge as the ball spun loose and responded angrily to Atletico coach Radomir Antic when he was substituted at the beginning of extra time.
Dani seemed to have sewn up the tie for Ajax with his superb long-distance strike midway through the first period of extra time.

However there was more in store in an action-packed final 20 minutes. Atletico replied swiftly when the unfortunate Veldman handled the ball during a tussle in the area and Pantic's firmly struck penalty just beat the diving Van der Sar.
With Ajax set to progress on the away goals rule Atletico threw everything forward and Radek Bejbl and Pantic went close in a frantic finale.
And with so many committed to attack Babangida and Dani combined to leave the Nigerian free to calmly lift the ball over Molina to settle the matter.
Atletico coach Radomir Antic was close to tears after seeing his side lose a game they could easily have won for the fourth time in just 10 days.

"We were really far superior. Bad luck - that's the easiest way to explain it...I am left with a sensation that in the semifinal there will not be a better team - that Atletico Madrid are better than Ajax," said Antic.
Equally emotional was Atletico owner Jesus Gil, who said: "I'm really proud of my team."
Atletico have seen their hopes in both the domestic and continental Cup competitions evaporate in less than two weeks as their league recovery also came off the rails.
Ajax meanwhile can eye their third successive final - but must first overcome Juventus.
